prompt:
A desktop website home page for the design portfolio of David Doctor, a UX and product design student, rendered edge to edge with crisp, readable text and no browser window, device or desk around it. Visitors are design recruiters deciding in seconds whether to open his work, so the two projects lead the screen.

Frame: an always-visible left sidebar holds the wordmark "David Doctor", then a cascade of four menu bars, each stepping slightly further right and tilted a few degrees: Home, Doctor's Brew, Buff Life, Resume. Home is the current page: a plate is stamped behind it, with a small solid triangle pointer at its left. A "My LinkedIn" button sits at the sidebar's foot.

Page, in reading order: a compact intro with a headshot of a smiling young man, the heading "Hey! I'm David Doctor" and the sentence "I'm a designer, developer, and analyst studying Information Science at the University of Colorado Boulder. Here are my projects that reflect my interests in branding, UI design, and digital experiences." Then the heading "Projects" and two large project tiles: "Package Design", showing the red Doctor's Brew beer logo, with "Box, bottle, and branding designs for a specialty pepper beer inspired by Filipino culture." and a "View Project" button; and "App Design", showing the Buff Life app logo, with "A mobile app concept designed to help CU Boulder students manage schedules, events, and campus life." and "View Project".

Visual law: the category standard for a contemporary designer portfolio, executed at full craft. A white ground, near-black text, and one confident blue accent used only for the selected menu item and the buttons; generous whitespace; large project images in simple tiles; one modern neutral sans throughout.
